searches.label: r3c2
searches.name: Global scale-5 frames, lr 2.5e-3
searches.hypothesis: Change: the r1c1 head (one global 8-frame softmax at scale 5) with lr 2.5e-3. Why: r1c1 matched r1c4 at lr 1.5e-3 and had the highest single seed (0.971). If lr 2.5e-3 helps it as it helped the per-type head, it may beat 0.969. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.969, or a seed collapses, which would show the scale-5 global mixture is less robust at high lr.

searches.label: r3c1
searches.name: 8-frame pool, lr 3e-3
searches.hypothesis: This is r2c1 with lr raised from 2.5e-3 to 3e-3. Going from 1.5e-3 to 2.5e-3 lifted the weak seed from 0.54 to 0.97, and lr 3e-3 with 3 epochs had no collapse. Faster learning within the fixed sample budget may push both seeds closer to 1. Refuted if the mean falls below 0.964 or either seed falls below 0.9 or collapses to 0.078.

searches.label: r3c4
searches.name: r1c1 recipe, entropy 0.01
searches.hypothesis: This keeps r1c1 exactly but doubles ent_coef from 0.005 to 0.01. The weak seeds had low training success, which points to slow learning, possibly from committing early to a poor policy over 257 actions. More entropy keeps exploration going while the frame mixture settles, and should lift the seed minimum. It is refuted if the mean falls below 0.90 or training success falls, which would mean the extra entropy only blurs the greedy policy.

searches.label: r3c4
searches.name: lr 2.5e-3, 256 envs x 8 steps
searches.hypothesis: This keeps r2c2 but collects each update from 256 parallel worlds over 8 steps instead of 128 worlds over 16. The update size (2048 samples), minibatch size (64) and number of updates stay the same. Each update then sees twice as many distinct designs, so gradients are less correlated. Fewer envs (64) hurt in 3 of 4 earlier worlds, which hints that more envs may help. Refuted if either seed falls below 0.92 or the mean is below r2c2's 0.949.

searches.label: r3c3
searches.name: Per-type mixture, lr 2.5e-3
searches.hypothesis: Change: r1c4's per-type [T, frames] softmax at scale 2, with lr raised to 2.5e-3. Why: r1c4 hit 0.977 on one seed but its other seed was slow (0.48). The same lr raise took the shared-mixture head from 0.91 to 0.96, so it may rescue the slow seed. Refuted if either seed is below 0.9 or the mean is below 0.958, which would mean the softer per-type mixture adds fragility.

searches.label: r3c4
searches.name: r1c1 + entropy 0.01
searches.hypothesis: This is r1c1 (2 epochs, lr 1.5e-3, 242k samples) with the entropy coefficient doubled to 0.01. More samples plus sustained exploration may lift the weaker r1c1 seed (0.918) and guard against the 0.47 plateau seen with neighbouring recipes. Paired with candidate 1, it tests whether entropy helps under either recipe. It is supported if the mean is above 0.936 with the minimum seed at least 0.93. It is refuted if either seed falls below 0.9.

searches.label: r3c3
searches.name: Window head, lr 1e-3, mixture scale 3
searches.hypothesis: Change: the r2c1 recipe (lr 1e-3, 32 minibatches) with the 16-way frame/order mixture softened from scale 5 to scale 3. Why: the seed gap (0.47 vs 0.83) may come from the mixture locking onto a frame too early. A softer softmax keeps alternatives alive longer, and soft mixtures saved a collapsing world before. Refuted if the weaker seed is not above 0.47 or the mean is not above 0.65.
